sm11-8.flavorText: Forests where Swadloon live have superb foliage because the nutrients they make from fallen leaves nourish the plant life.

sm11-10.flavorText: It makes a hole in a suitable rock. If that rock breaks, the Pokémon remains agitated until it locates a replacement.

abilities.name: Shell Armor

sm11-11.flavorText: It possesses legs of enormous strength, enabling it to carry heavy slabs for many days, even when crossing arid land.

attacks.name: Take Down

sm11-12.flavorText: These mysterious Pokémon evolve when they receive electrical stimulation while they are in the same place as Shelmet.

attacks.name: Spore

sm11-13.flavorText: It lures people in with its Poké Ball pattern, then releases poison spores. Why it resembles a Poké Ball is unknown.

attacks.name: Venoshock

abilities.name: Bursting Spores
abilities.text: Whenever you play a Pokémon that has the Spore attack from your hand during your turn, you may leave your opponent's Active Pokémon Asleep and Poisoned.

sm11-14.flavorText: They show off their Poké Ball caps to lure prey, but very few Pokémon are fooled by this.

attacks.name: Sweet Scent
attacks.text: Heal 30 damage from 1 of your Pokémon.

sm11-15.flavorText: When the sun rises, Fomantis spreads its four leaves and bathes in the sunlight. The tip of its head has a pleasant aroma.

attacks.name: Petal Blizzard
attacks.text: This attack does 10 damage to each of your opponent's Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

attacks.name: Sol Slice
attacks.text: If this Pokémon has any Fire Energy attached to it, this attack does 50 more damage.

sm11-16.flavorText: For self-protection, it pretends to be a bug Pokémon. Both of its arms bear keen-edged petals.

sm11-17.flavorText: Because of its sweet, delicious aroma, bird Pokémon are always after it, but it's not intelligent enough to care.

attacks.name: Double Slap
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 30 damage for each heads.

sm11-18.flavorText: It's protected by its hard sepals, so it plays with bird Pokémon without worry. They peck it relentlessly, but it doesn't care.

abilities.name: Queenly Reward

sm11-19.flavorText: A master of grand and beautiful kicks, it can knock out even kickboxing champions with a single blow.

sm11-20.flavorText: It wraps its prey in green seaweed and sucks away their vitality. It only likes to go after big prey like Wailord.

attacks.name: Smoke Bomb

sm11-21.flavorText: Its entire body is burning. When it breathes, the temperature rises. When it sneezes, flames shoot out!

attacks.name: Smoke Bomb
attacks.text: If the Defending Pokémon tries to attack during your opponent's next turn, your opponent flips a coin. If tails, that attack doesn't happen.

sm11-22.flavorText: There are still quite a few factories that rely on the flames provided by Magmortar to process metals.

sm11-23.flavorText: Its humped back stores intensely hot magma. In rain, the magma cools, slowing its movement.

sm11-24.flavorText: The volcanoes on its back have a major eruption every 10 years—or whenever it becomes really angry.

sm11-26.flavorText: This Pokémon brings victory. It is said that Trainers with Victini always win, regardless of the type of encounter.

attacks.name: Find a Friend

sm11-27.flavorText: While shining a light and pretending to be a guide, it leeches off the life force of any who follow it.

sm11-29.flavorText: The spirits it absorbs fuel its baleful fire. It hangs around hospitals waiting for people to pass on.

sm11-30.flavorText: Being consumed in Chandelure's flame burns up the spirit, leaving the body behind.

attacks.name: Flame Charge
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Fire Energy card and attach it to this Pokémon. Then, shuffle your deck.

sm11-31.flavorText: It scatters embers in the tall grass. Then bug Pokémon, frightened by the flames, come flying out, and Fletchinder gobbles them up.

attacks.name: Heat Wave

attacks.name: Flare Raid

sm11-32.flavorText: Its tough wings don't allow fire to pass through them. A long time ago, firefighters' outfits were made from Talonflame wings.

sm11-33.flavorText: The males will do whatever the females tell them. They give the females most of their food. Due to malnutrition, the males can't evolve.

sm11-34.flavorText: Salazzle lives deep in caves and forces the Salandit it has attracted with its pheromones to serve it.

attacks.name: Ditch and Splash

attacks.name: Thrilling Times-GX
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 100 more damage. If this Pokémon has at least 6 extra Water Energy attached to it (in addition to this attack's cost), flip 10 coins instead, and this attack does 100 more damage for each heads. (You can't use more than 1 GX attack in a game.)

abilities.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), you may put a Misty's Favor card from your discard pile into your hand.

sm11-36.flavorText: It likes swimming around with people on its back. In the Alola region, it's an important means of transportation over water.

sm11-37.flavorText: It feeds mainly on ice and snow. It's only able to survive in a limited number of places in the warm Alola region.

attacks.name: Spiteful Sigh
attacks.text: Put up to 7 damage counters on this Pokémon. This attack does 20 damage for each damage counter you placed in this way.

attacks.name: Icy Wind
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Asleep.

sm11-38.flavorText: It freezes hikers who have come to climb snowy mountains and carries them back to its home. It only goes after men it thinks are handsome.

sm11-39.flavorText: When night falls, their pink patterns begin to shine. They're popular with divers, so there are resorts that feed them to keep them close.

attacks.name: Neon Trickery
attacks.text: You may move an Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon to 1 of their Benched Pokémon.

sm11-40.flavorText: Deep down at the bottom of the ocean, prey is scarce. Lumineon get into fierce disputes with Lanturn over food.

attacks.name: Powder Snow
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Asleep.

sm11-41.flavorText: During cold seasons, it migrates to the mountain's lower reaches. It returns to the snow-covered summit in the spring.

attacks.name: Quick Freeze
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon has any Water Energy attached to it, it is now Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Wild Tackle
attacks.text: This Pokémon does 20 damage to itself.

sm11-42.flavorText: It blankets wide areas in snow by whipping up blizzards. It is also known as "The Ice Monster."

attacks.name: Swarming Bites
attacks.text: This attack does 20 damage for each Basculin you have in play to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

sm11-43.flavorText: Savage, violent Pokémon, red and blue Basculin are always fighting each other over territory.

sm11-44.flavorText: It was restored from an ancient fossil. Tirtouga lived in the sea but came up onto the land to search for prey.

attacks.name: Aqua Impact
attacks.text: This attack does 20 more damage for each Colorless in your opponent's Active Pokémon's Retreat Cost.

abilities.name: Ancient Custom
abilities.text: Pokémon Tool cards attached to your opponent's Pokémon have no effect.

sm11-45.flavorText: Its jaws are terrifyingly powerful. It could eat Omastar and Omanyte whole and not be bothered in the slightest by their shells.

attacks.name: Frozen Lock

sm11-46.flavorText: They are born in snow clouds. They use chains made of ice crystals to capture prey.

sm11-51.flavorText: The shell covering its body is as hard as diamond. This Pokémon will do anything it takes to win.

sm11-52.flavorText: The tradition known as Pyukumuku chucking started from the custom of throwing Pyukumuku back into the sea after they wash onshore.

sm11-57.flavorText: It focuses psychic energy into its tail and rides it like it's surfing. Another name for this Pokémon is "hodad."

attacks.name: Supersonic

sm11-58.flavorText: It's frequently the cause of power outages, which is why some power plants send out electrical signals that it can't stand.

attacks.text: Discard all Lightning Energy from this Pokémon. This attack does 30 damage for each card you discarded in this way.

sm11-66.flavorText: With their sucker mouths, they suck in prey. Then they use their fangs to shock the prey with electricity.

sm11-67.flavorText: Its skin is very hard, so it is unhurt even if stepped on by sumo wrestlers. It smiles when transmitting electricity.

attacks.name: Thunderous Gale

attacks.name: Raging Thunder

sm11-68.flavorText: The spikes on its tail discharge immense bolts of lightning. It flies around the Unova region firing off lightning bolts.

attacks.name: Nature Dive

sm11-69.flavorText: Although it's called a guardian deity, if a person or Pokémon puts it in a bad mood, it will become a malevolent deity and attack.

sm11-70.flavorText: Although it's alien to this world and a danger here, it's apparently a common organism in the world where it normally lives.

sm11-75.flavorText: The rich greenery of the Alola region is hard on Marowak. It controls fire to stay alive.

attacks.name: Attract Smack
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

sm11-76.flavorText: It sways its hips to a rhythm all its own. The precise movements of Jynx living in Alola are truly wonderful.

sm11-77.flavorText: It tends to move in a pack with others. They cluster in a tight group to sleep in a cave.

sm11-81.flavorText: There's a rumor that if you catch a Drifblim floating on the wind at dusk, you'll be carried away to the afterlife.

attacks.name: Knock Off
attacks.text: Discard a random card from your opponent's hand.

sm11-82.flavorText: It grips prey with its tail claws and injects poison. It tenaciously hangs on until the poison takes.

abilities.name: Secret Territory
abilities.text: If you have Mesprit and Azelf in play, apply Weakness for each Pokémon (both yours and your opponent's) as ×4 instead.

sm11-83.flavorText: Known as "The Being of Knowledge." It is said that it can wipe out the memory of those who see its eyes.

attacks.name: First Contact
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 3 Basic Pokémon and put them onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

sm11-84.flavorText: Known as "The Being of Emotion." It taught humans the nobility of sorrow, pain, and joy.

sm11-85.flavorText: Known as "The Being of Willpower." It sleeps at the bottom of a lake to keep the world in balance.

abilities.name: Dimension Breach

sm11-86.flavorText: This Pokémon is said to live in a world on the reverse side of ours, where common knowledge is distorted and strange.

attacks.name: Aurora Gain

sm11-87.flavorText: Shiny particles are released from its wings like a veil. It is said to represent the crescent moon.

sm11-88.flavorText: This Pokémon appears before people and Pokémon who are having nightmares and eats those dreams.

attacks.name: Rest Well

sm11-89.flavorText: The mist emanating from their foreheads is packed with the dreams of people and Pokémon.

sm11-90.flavorText: It controls tremendous psychic power. Most reports of alien sightings are actually just people mistaking Elgyem for an alien.

sm11-91.flavorText: With its psychic powers, it rewrites its opponents' memories. You, too, may have already had your memories rewritten.

sm11-137.flavorText: They move in small groups, walking around lazily. Anyone who makes eye contact gets smacked with a headbutt.

attacks.name: Turf Raid

sm11-144.flavorText: This nuisance sneaks into people's homes, where it hides important things and scatters cotton all over the place.

sm11-156.flavorText: They are kind but can be relentless when defending territory. They challenge foes with tusks that can cut steel.

sm11-162.flavorText: A contest is under way to determine which one can stick its tongue out the farthest. The current record is…more than 82 feet.

sm11-170.flavorText: The world's laziest Pokémon. It moves to another spot when there's no food left within its reach.

sm11-174.flavorText: This very forgetful Pokémon will wait for a new order from its Trainer even though it already has one.

attacks.name: Air Slash

sm11-175.flavorText: Many people believe that, deep in the forest where Tranquill live, there is a peaceful place where there is no war.

sm11-176.flavorText: Males swing their head plumage to threaten opponents. The females' flying abilities surpass those of the males.

attacks.name: Thunderous Tornado

sm11-179.flavorText: While it's an amiable Pokémon, if you touch it unexpectedly, it will heat up its body in an instant, and you'll be burned.

sm11-180.flavorText: Its stomach takes up most of its long torso. It's a big eater, so the amount Trainers have to spend on its food is no laughing matter.

sm11-181.flavorText: Although it wasn't originally found in Alola, this Pokémon was brought over a long time ago when there was a huge Rattata outbreak.

attacks.name: Quick Blow
